A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EasyHOI work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v3 reports original reconstruction experiments on Arctic, OakInk, and DexYCB, grasp simulations, optimization ablations, and qualitative results on collected images.

after.justification: v4 retains those experiments and adds original hand-accuracy results, component comparisons, runtime measurements, and failure-case evaluations.

M1.justification: The reconstruction pipeline, three-stage optimization, losses, and contact-selection procedure remain unchanged in Sections 3, 7, and 8. Tripo3D was already tested in v3; the new HODet and ground-truth-object experiments evaluate alternatives and controls without changing the proposed method.

E1.justification: v4 adds evaluation on MOW, illustrated through failures involving motion blur and ambiguous grasps in Section 9.4 and Figure 15. Arctic, OakInk, DexYCB, and collected in-the-wild images were already covered in v3; the additional measurements on them do not establish new coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same four baselines. v4 adds HaMeR as a standalone hand-accuracy comparator and HODet with SAM as a segmentation comparator. Figure 13 also adds comparisons against IHOI, AlignSDF, gSDF, and MOHO on previously illustrated in-the-wild examples. These are targeted extensions of the existing comparison suite.

E3.justification: Evaluation substantially expands to a previously unmeasured output: hand accuracy using MPVPE and MPJPE, with predicted-object and ground-truth-object controls. v4 also introduces segmentation-IoU evaluation using SAM on HODet boxes and a runtime study over 65 images. The original sampling procedure, zero-shot exclusions, and optimization budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds diagnostic comparisons of LISA versus HODet/SAM and quantifies dependence on InstantMesh, Tripo3D, and ground-truth geometry in Table 5. It extends the existing loss ablation with hand-error measurements and adds OakInk and MOW failure analyses. These substantially broaden the investigation beyond v3's retained stage, loss, inpainting, and qualitative reconstruction-model analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations for simulation displacement and intersection volume in the stage and loss ablations. v4 retains this reporting and provides no new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-test information. The 65-image runtime sample is not a repeated-run count.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the existing ablation values are unchanged, but substantial results are added. Table 2 newly reports OakInk MPJPE of 1.03 cm for HaMeR, 1.22 for EasyHOI with predicted objects, and 0.77 with ground-truth objects. Further additions include hand-error ablations, object-quality comparisons, LISA versus HODet/SAM IoU of 0.74 versus 0.61, runtime measurements, and qualitative comparisons and failures.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(8), the MANO parameterization, and the supplementary contact-mask and ray-intersection definitions are retained. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: single-image HOI reconstruction using large-model priors and prior-guided optimization, with strong generalization, physical plausibility, and baseline superiority. The added evidence does not revise these central statements.

C2.justification: v4 introduces a substantive trade-off between physical plausibility and hand accuracy when object geometry is imperfect, supported by predicted-versus-ground-truth comparisons. It expands v3's generic model-failure caveat with explanations involving inpainting artifacts, segmentation errors, motion blur, and ambiguous grasps, and proposes more specific remedies in Section 9.4.

D1.justification: Section 9.1 newly documents runtime by processing stage, averaged over 65 images: 58.97 seconds for initial reconstruction and 57.03 seconds for optimization. The added segmentation comparison explains how HODet boxes are converted into masks using SAM. Existing hardware, optimization hyperparameters, and project-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The related-work survey and novelty positioning remain unchanged. The additional bibliography entry, v4 reference 53, duplicates Shan et al.'s 2020 work already listed as reference 52 in both versions; it does not introduce a distinct cited work.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained, with localized corrections and an expanded quantitative-results discussion. Supplementary Section 9 is reorganized into runtime, model ablation, qualitative comparison, and failure-analysis subsections, including relocation of the existing reconstruction-model discussion.

P2.justification: v4 substantially extends the result displays with new Tables 2 and 5, new Figures 12-15, and hand-error columns in the loss-ablation table. Existing figures are retained, with some resizing and layout reflow. v3 Figures 12-15 correspond to v4 Figures 16-19 rather than being removed.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses an important evaluation gap: v3's object and grasp metrics did not establish hand-pose accuracy. Tables 2 and 5 now expose the accuracy cost of imperfect object geometry and test the optimizer with ground-truth objects. Specific failure analyses and runtime measurements further clarify practical limitations. Although the abstract's broad superiority claim remains insufficiently qualified, the added diagnostic evidence substantially improves empirical completeness and transparency.
